title: Electronics Cap on Re-Settlement After Recovery (Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan)
content:
These questions are answered from the electronics rule for re-settling a Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan claim after stolen property is recovered.

**What caps electronics on a re-settlement?**
The re-settlement's electronics cap: the level's electronics sublimit multiplied by 1.5 when the covered unit's class includes an individual door alarm, by 1.25 when the class has no door alarm and no drive-up access, and by 1 otherwise. It applies to the electronics still missing and to the electronics before recovery alike.

**Where are the unit features read?**
From the unit class of the covered Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement: whether the class includes an individual door alarm, and whether it has drive-up access.

**Which multiplier applies to a drive-up unit without a door alarm?**
1 — the sublimit itself.

**A worked figure (hypothetical).** An electronics sublimit of 1,120.00 in a unit class with no door alarm and no drive-up access gives a cap of 1,400.00; with a door alarm, 1,680.00.
